subject: Extremely high precision estimates for rw2 and inla.hyperpar crashes

messages.author: 80b903b54c9cf4bd
messages.subject: Extremely high precision estimates for rw2 and inla.hyperpar crashes
parts:
Hi,

I was running a spatio-temporal model for the last 5 days and finally it finishes. Everything looks good except for the precision estimates for a random effect, which was given a rw2 prior. The posterior mean is 1.324056e+05 and mode is 939.4771766. The density plot looks wired and the inla.hyperpar function can't be successfully used. Can I fix the problem instead of rerun the model? Here are some details.

The part related to the random effect is:
#uniform on standard deviation U[0, +inf] 
sdunif = "expression:
logdens = -log_precision/2;
return(logdens)"
#the formular is
res_zero_inflacated= Y ~ <some parts> + f(age_group.y, model='rw2', constr=TRUE,
    hyper = list(prec = list(prior=sdunif)))
Here are some plots for the parameter:
first is the plot of the rw2 random variable (is that because it is actually very linear so that rw2 will fail?):




plot(res_zero_inflacated$marginals.hyperpar$`Precision for age_group.y`, type='l')


> plot(log(res_zero_inflacated$internal.marginals.hyperpar$`Log precision for age_group.y`), type='l')
Warning message:
In log(res_zero_inflacated$internal.marginals.hyperpar$`Log precision for age_group.y`) :  NaNs produced




I tried to use 
result_refined = inla.hyperpar(res_zero_inflacated , dz = 0.2 , diff.logdens =20,verbose = TRUE)
but inla crashed with the following errors many times:
GMRFLib version 3.0-0-snapshot, has recived error no [9]                               
        Reason    : Invalid value of parameter                                          
        Message   : Condition `n >= (int) gsl_interp_linear->min_size' is not TRUE      
        Function  : GMRFLib_density_interp_type                                       
        GMRFLib version 3.0-0-snapshot, has recived error no [9]                        
        Reason    : Invalid value of parameter                                          
        Message   : Condition `n >= (int) gsl_interp_linear->min_size' is not TRUE      
        Function  : GMRFLib_density_interp_type                                         
        File      : density.c

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Extremely high precision estimates for rw2 and inla.hyperpar crashes
parts:
On Wed, 2017-12-20 at 00:17 -0800, Jiang Du wrote:
> Thank you for the comments. However,
> What if I want to show the posterior variance？it looks wired:
>

> plot.default(inla.tmarginal(function(x) 1/x,
> res_zero_inflacated$marginals.hyperpar[[4]]), type =
> 'l')#theprecisionparameter is in the[[4]] position
>
> Is there a way to produce a better looking variance density?

_always_ compute transformed densitites from the internal representation, so do

inla.tmarginal(function(x) 1/exp(x),
res_zero_inflacated$internal.marginals.hyperpar[[4]]),


and you'll be fine.

--
Håvard Rue
Helpdesk
he...@r-inla.org

On Wed, 2017-12-20 at 09:10 -0800, Jiang Du wrote:
> It's my first time knowing that. Now the density looks acceptable.
>

the reason for this is that the densities are more gaussian-like in
this scale. as we use a finite representation, we loose accuracy moving
trough a transformation making it severely skewed or non-Gaussian
looking.
